what_happened: The job was asked to check the ontology terms in docs/ontology.toml against the governing sources they summarize. The verifier rejected it with one major finding and no failed checks named. The check lets an entry carry a "source-only" excuse that switches off the content check for the whole file. Six of the seven terms (planning, job, Athena, product versus system, landed, Sri) use that excuse on every file that gets scanned. So only Hermes, the case that was already fixed, is actually compared with its sources. The check exists in form but does almost no checking.
cause: The check's design allowed an exemption with file-wide scope and no bound on how often it could be used. No criterion or test measured coverage, such as how many terms are really compared against their sources. The check could therefore be met by excusing entries instead of checking them, and only the final verifier looked at what the excuses did. This is a sibling of the gate-exemption-by-declared-phrase class (2m6a), but the cause here is an unbounded per-file excuse in a content check, not a phrase that skips a threshold. It is not the same as that class, so I did not tag it.
prevention: Make the ontology test narrow the excuse so it applies to one named claim or file and requires a stated reason. The test should also fail when the share of terms that are really checked against a source falls below a stated floor. Here that floor is every term having at least one claim compared with its governing source text. Add a test that takes a term whose definition contradicts its source and shows the check fails, to prove that the excuse does not hide it.
proposed_request: Fix the ontology check so it compares every term in docs/ontology.toml with the governing sources it summarizes. Outcome: a source-only excuse may skip a single named file for a term only when it gives a written reason, and it never turns off the content check for the term as a whole. Each of the seven terms (Hermes, planning, job, Athena, product versus system, landed, Sri) must have at least one claim checked against its governing source text. Acceptance: (1) a test fails when a term's definition contradicts its source, for each of the seven terms, using a deliberately altered definition; (2) a test fails if any term has no checked claim, or if an excuse has no reason or covers more than one named file; (3) the existing ontology tests and `cargo test --locked` pass; (4) any term whose definition really disagrees with its source is corrected in docs/ontology.toml, with the change listed. Do not change production code outside the ontology test and docs/ontology.toml.
